tasks.short: Develop geothermal operating plans and schedules

steps.what: Establish operating objectives, well constraints and maintenance windows
inputs: existing well limits and operating requirements

steps.what: Construct operating schedule options against the validated constraints
outputs: feasible schedule drafts and unresolved conflicts

steps.what: Review operational risks and select the operating plan and schedule
inputs: feasible schedule drafts and unresolved conflicts

steps.what: Prepare the operating plan document with scheduled activities and responsibilities
Check and approve the final operating plan and schedule
Save the approved operating plan in the current planning record

tasks.design: Configure constraint-based schedule drafting in {OPS_SYSTEM}, then assemble the selected plan into {DOCS}. The manager validates constraints, resolves operating trade-offs and approves the completed plan; no schedule is pushed to plant controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedule construction can involve repeated conflict checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic scheduling can test explicit constraints and expose unsatisfied ones.
tasks.still_hard: Set valid operating constraints and judge unusual plant conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Accept the operational plan and its risks.

ambition.what: Compare operating schedules when constraints change.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5; planning access and applicable staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: deterministic schedulers can check explicit resource and time constraints without controlling a plant.

assumptions: Boundary is developing plans and schedules, not issuing instructions or changing PLC settings.

s1 counts capturing approved well/plant limits, required tasks, dependencies, allowable windows and objectives. Existing maintenance and roster owners already supply asset/task IDs, duration, availability and qualifications. Missing constraints return to manual planning; none are inferred by a model.

s3 counts selecting activities, timing, owners and recorded exceptions; s4 copies these into a plan template. Native scheduling and templates come first. Central retains 40% of schedule construction and 70% of document preparation, with all decisions and review unchanged.
Same-system save is effectively zero; minimum 1 earns no saving. Edits invalidate the approval, which follows final document creation.
Provisional B=100, R=81.7, gross=18.3; focal upkeep=1.3; net=17, independent of means priors.
unknowns: Constraint completeness and manual conflict effort
research_questions: Replay past schedules using only constraints that were available at planning time.

incremental.description: Maintain planning constraints and regression-check schedule rules

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: native planning already covers the work. High: 18.3 hours of reduction face five extra conflict hours and 1.3 upkeep hours, leaving 12.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain geothermal operating logs and reports

steps.what: Capture actual operational events and maintenance explanations not present in instrument logs
Gather daily instrument, shift and maintenance records and reconcile missing or duplicate entries
Assemble daily logs, maintenance references and event notes into the report
Review daily logs and report content and approve the final records
Save the approved daily records in the current operations record
Maintain the records by resolving later verified corrections and preserving their history
outputs: maintained geothermal records with correction history

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} record gathering and a deterministic {DOCS} daily report using actual logs and manager-entered explanations. The manager reviews the complete records before saving them and remains responsible for later corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instrument logs and maintenance explanations may need manual collation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record links and report templates can assemble existing actuals without writing fictional event explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Establish what actually happened when log entries conflict or are incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: Validate operational meaning and correct the record.

ambition.what: Keep traceable daily records with less manual assembly.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-4; operations permissions and applicable staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: instrument and maintenance records can be assembled with deterministic templates when source IDs and timestamps are available.

assumptions: Boundary includes recording actual events, gathering, reviewing and maintaining logs and reports. No saving is assigned to the PLC's existing automatic logging runtime.

Existing instruments supply tag, timestamp, value, unit and quality flag. Maintenance staff already record asset/work-order ID, actual action, completion time and outcome. s1 counts manager capture of event ID, observed time, factual explanation, source and uncertainty; missing facts remain unresolved rather than inferred from a plan.

s2 performs source gathering/linking and exception handling; s3 performs template assembly. Native features come first. Central retains 40% of gathering and 30% of report assembly effort; record review and correction stay fully human.
Same-record save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Final review follows report creation and any edit invalidates approval. Later manual corrections retain their full effort.
Provisional B=100, R=71, gross=29; focal upkeep=1; net=28, independent of means priors.
research_questions: Reconcile several daily reports to raw logs and maintenance records and measure all correction time.

already_counted.description: Resolve missing and duplicate source entries

incremental.description: Check source mapping changes and audit report completeness

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: existing native reporting already does the assembly. High: 29 gross points require six extra source-exception hours plus one upkeep hour, leaving 22.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor geothermal operations through PLC displays

steps.what: Observe geothermal operations on the programmable logic controller displays
inputs: existing live PLC displays and alarms

steps.what: Interpret operating trends and alarms against current plant conditions
Record and confirm the monitoring observation requiring follow-up
Save the approved monitoring observation in its current log

tasks.design: Retain the manager's monitoring and interpretation through {OPS_SYSTEM}, the existing PLC interface. Separate the manager's observation note from automatic telemetry; the latter is already machine work and supplies no labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The monitoring task already relies on automated sensing and displays.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional mechanism establishes less required human monitoring.
tasks.still_hard: Interpret abnormal trends in the current operating context.

ambition.what: Preserve effective supervision of existing automated controls.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: PLC sensing and control runtime is already automated and is distinct from a manager's monitoring labour.

assumptions: Boundary includes monitoring interpretation and its observation note. Control adjustments, repairs and daily report assembly are separate tasks; no note write is hidden in screen observation.

PLC tag values, timestamps, units and alarm states are existing instrument outputs. The manager captures actual observation time, affected tags, assessment and follow-up need in s3; no new feed is assumed.
Native displays and alarm features are already considered. A further dashboard does not by itself justify reduced monitoring or note-writing effort.
Same-log save is approximately zero; minimum 1 is retained and its gate follows the completed note. Provisional B=100, R=100, gross=0; incremental=0; net=0. Shares are independent of the prior.
unknowns: Whether required monitoring duration can change with an approved operating procedure
research_questions: Observe required human monitoring separately from instrument and control runtime.

incremental.description: No additional monitoring system or upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Existing PLC automation is already in the baseline; no reduction in human monitoring, interpretation or actual note capture is established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare the assessment route and retrieve the applicable well-field maps and prior findings
inputs: existing well-field map and well identifiers

steps.what: Conduct the well-field site inspection and observe access, equipment and field conditions
Capture actual well-field observations, measurements and located photographs
Assess the site evidence and record conclusions and unresolved concerns
Assemble the site evidence and conclusions into the assessment report
Check the report against site evidence and approve its final version
Save the approved assessment in its current site record

tasks.design: Configure well-linked references and field-evidence capture in {OPS_SYSTEM}, then assemble the captured evidence and manager-written conclusions in {DOCS}. The site visit, actual measurement capture, assessment judgement and final report review retain their full effort.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessment preparation and report assembly can be separate from field evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Native well identifiers and field templates can link existing references and actual observations.
tasks.still_hard: Assess the significance of field conditions and incomplete evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Conduct the visit and accept its conclusions.

ambition.what: Reduce preparation and report assembly around a complete site assessment.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3; site evidence access and applicable staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: site templates can assemble located evidence and human-written conclusions into reports.

assumptions: Boundary includes the field visit and written assessment. No travel, observation or measurement time is removed by a record view.

Existing map/asset owners supply well ID, location, revision and prior finding references. Missing links require manual preparation in s1. s3 explicitly counts capture of observed time, well/location, actual reading and unit, photo, finding and uncertainty; s4 produces the actual assessment conclusions.
Native reference views and report templates come first. Central removes 30% of preparation navigation and half of report formatting/assembly only; no model generates conclusions.
Same-record save is effectively zero; minimum 1 earns no saving. Approval follows the final assembled report and edits invalidate it.
Provisional B=100, R=93, gross=7; focal upkeep=1; net=6. Shares are independent of means priors.
research_questions: Compare captured site evidence with final assessment reports and time all manual handling.

already_counted.description: Verify the assembled report against actual site evidence

incremental.description: Maintain site templates and check missing evidence mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: native assessment tools already cover the work. High: seven hours of handling reduction need two extra evidence-exception hours and one upkeep hour, leaving four.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain geothermal operational judgement and field work while improving supported planning and record assembly.
reach: Maintenance team: preserve actual action records
Control engineers: separate existing telemetry from manager labour
role.ambitious_version: A geothermal manager who plans from explicit constraints and reviews traceable records while retaining plant supervision and field assessment.
